correctness.rationale: Inverse windows are precisely abba; two windows give the same parent only within a constant run (published collision equations). Thus each long constant run and each matching-color-flanked interior double run contributes exactly one distinct parent. Weighted run transitions yield the rational generating function by exact formal algebra. A nondegenerate dominant simple pole at t=1 gives the stated mean slope, positive variance slope and Gaussian limit by analytic quasi-powers. The independent enumeration within the supplied package matches all three descriptions on 222456 words. Finite verification is corroborative and not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Relevant primary results and prior mathematical records cover binary run populations, general-alphabet inverse-degree extremality and incidence, and even-length channel conjugacy; none of the inspected material gives the full nonbinary inverse-list distribution together with a proved positive-variance Gaussian limit. The distinction is substantive: q>=3 run colors require a return-to-the-preprevious-color test. Indexed noncoverage is not a uniqueness theorem; see residual risks.
residual_risks: An older nonbinary palindrome sphere-size distribution could be expressed in a differently indexed transfer-matrix or pattern-counting formulation.
The inverse-list maximum, mean and binary histogram are pre-existing; novelty is limited to the nonbinary full distribution and its Gaussian refinement.
Independent research audit and exhaustive search of unpublished literature were not performed.

value.rationale: The new q-ary population law is a natural complete classification of receiving-word list ambiguity; it distinguishes run-color returns invisible for q=2 and determines every finite-length frequency including zero-parent words. The normal limit and explicit dispersion determine typical uncertainty, not implied by existing maximum bounds or aggregate incidence. No unmotivated fixed-size slice is proposed.
